stories.title: What is commoning? A systematic review of definitions, narratives and differences with the commons
stories.description: Research on commoning is expanding, but there is no unifying definition or conceptual framework. Numerous definitions and narratives of what commoning is or could be are observable across research fields and empirical contexts. How is commoning scholarship different or similar to literature on the commons? In this article, we systematically review the literature on commoning across all academic fields and topics. We examine 637 peer-reviewed articles that explicitly use the term and analyze the heterogeneity of definitions, narratives, and contexts associated with the concept. We identify five core commoning narratives, each represented by distinctive terminologies and phrases of how the term is defined in the literature. The five narratives are: (1) governance, (2) relationships, (3) normative goals, (4) economy, and (5) politics. Most definitions of commoning in the literature contain elements of multiple narratives. The degree to which the different narratives of commoning extend or significantly differ from concepts of the commons is also mixed. Governance narratives, for example, tend to position commoning as an extension of the social processes for governing commons, whereas the economic and political narratives tend to frame commoning as an oppositional form of social movements towards alternative futures, not necessarily related to traditional conceptions of the commons. We attempt to understand these narratives with both quantitative and qualitative analyses to examine a range of thematic interpretations of the literature from rethinking social organization or emphasizing power and politics to embracing alternative relational ethics. In doing so, we provide examples of selected empirical studies that align with each of the five narratives, and discuss the concept’s pluralism and potential future directions. This includes how commoning differs from commons and collective action theory in its disciplinary origins and normative orientation, as well as its actionable practice-based elements. Furthermore, we interpret the observed trends as the beginning of a turn in the research paradigm on social groups, collective action, and collaboration in society. This may also be associated with a stronger normative orientation of social change research for sustainability and transformation (i.e., to produce system, target, and transformative knowledge).

stories.title: Patulin degradation in apple juice during cold atmospheric plasma treatment: parametric screening and optimization
stories.description: Considering the need for obtaining high-quality food, it is crucial to work on approaches for juice processing. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP), generated by pulse-modulated radio-frequency flowing liquid electrode atmospheric pressure glow discharge (pm-rf-FLE-APGD), for the freshly-squeezed, unpasteurized apple juice (AJ) treatment. The methodology involved optimizing of the operat​ing working conditions using design of experiments (DoE) and subsequently evaluating the effects of the CAP treatment on patulin degradation, microbial inactivation, physicochemical properties and nutritional properties, as well as the formation of reactive oxygen and nitrogen ​species (RONS) and antioxidant activity of AJ with the use of the ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) assay. It was revealed that the pm-rf-FLE-APGD treatment of AJ led to the removal of the artificially introduced patulin up to 69 ± 1% and 100% elimination of all detected microorganisms in AJ. Additionally, subjection of AJ to pm-rf-FLE-APGD led to an increase in total phenolic concentration from 461.6 ± 0.6 to 566.5 ± 0.9 mg L−1 besides triggering a slight decrease of approximately 10% in the contents of AA. Finally, the concentrations of RONS in CAP-treated AJ increased significantly, with nitrite levels rising by 51% and the total reactive oxygen species (ROS) concentration increasing 27-fold. Additionally, a 2.8 times increase of FRAP value was observed for the CAP-treated AJ. Here we demonstrate the potential of pm-rf-FLE-APGD as a method for enhancing the microbial safety and preserving the quality of unpasteurized AJ.

stories.title: PGAM5 dephosphorylates LCLAT1S410 to trigger cardiolipin oxidation-driven ferroptosis in cadmium-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
stories.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represents a prevalent, steadily increasing metabolic liver disease characterized by steatosis and liver injury, with disease progression influenced by environmental risk factors. Cadmium (Cd), a ubiquitous environmental metal toxicant, has been epidemiologically associated with MASLD progression. Although mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative lipid damage contribute to MASLD pathogenesis, whether and how Cd disrupts mitochondrial lipid homeostasis to initiate lipid peroxidation-associated injury remains elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that cardiolipin (CL) oxidation-associated ferroptosis and hepatic lipid accumulation are markedly increased in Cd-exposed mouse livers in vivo and in Cd-treated hepatocytes in vitro, exacerbating liver injury and promoting MASLD progression. Integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic analyses revealed profound alterations in mitochondrial lipid metabolic pathways, highlighting CL remodeling as a key regulatory layer underlying oxidative lipid damage and ferroptosis-associated liver injury. Mechanistically, phosphoglycerate mutase family member 5 (PGAM5) functions as an upstream regulator. Cd exposure enhances mitochondrial PGAM5–lysocardiolipin acyltransferase 1 (LCLAT1) interaction, triggering PGAM5-dependent LCLAT1 dephosphorylation at serine 410 (S410), thereby reinforcing LCLAT1 mitochondrial translocation, accelerating CL acyl-chain remodeling, and driving CL oxidation-dependent ferroptosis. Pharmacological or genetic PGAM5 inhibition attenuated CL oxidation, ferroptosis, and MASLD-like liver injury in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, PGAM5 and LCLAT1 are upregulated and positively correlated in human MASLD livers. Collectively, these findings define a PGAM5–LCLAT1–CL axis linking cadmium exposure to mitochondria-driven ferroptosis and MASLD progression, and identify PGAM5 as a potential therapeutic target for environmentally associated MASLD.
